methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $100M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median

private.name: Humanoid

data.narrative:
Apptronik is a Series A-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Jeff Cardenas that has raised $935M+. The valuation assessment draws on a peer universe of 9 comparable companies spanning private venture-backed firms (Humanoid, Bedrock Robotics, Dexterity, Walden Robotics, Generalist AI) and one public comparable, providing triangulation across stage-adjacent and sector-aligned benchmarks.

Two methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the $100M total-raised proxy as a base, applying a 2.0x Series A step-up multiplier typical of progression to the next funding round, implying a $200M valuation. Peer-median analysis across five same-sector comparables at Series A and adjacent stages yields a $1.6B median, with a range of $1.1B (Walden Robotics, Seed) to $2.0B (Generalist AI, Series B). The peer set reflects stage variance, with Series B companies valued at $1.8B–$2.0B and Series A comparable Humanoid at $1.4B.

Triangulation across both methods supports a valuation range of $170M (low) to $1.9B (high), with a median of $925M. The wide dispersion reflects material uncertainty in stage-adjusted comparables and limited precedent for Series A robotics companies at scale. Key risk factors include the relevance of later-stage Series B peer valuations and whether Apptronik's capital intensity and progress warrant positioning at the upper or lower end of peer ranges.
